long_simulate — DRIVE long op

• Data kinds: scalar × scalar × any → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.long_simulate(s0: 'float', v0: 'float', command: 'Callable', road=None, t_end: 'float' = 30.0, dt: 'float' = 0.01, params: 'Optional[dict]' = None, t_breaks: 'Sequence[float]' = (), t0: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import drivelong; drivelong.long_simulate(s0: 'float', v0: 'float', command: 'Callable', road=None, t_end: 'float' = 30.0, dt: 'float' = 0.01, params: 'Optional[dict]' = None, t_breaks: 'Sequence[float]' = (), t0: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("long_simulate"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Integrates the longitudinal equation of motion with RK4 (steps are split at event times; see the module docstring).

Parameters

s0, v0 : initial position [m] (arc length along the road) and speed [m/s] (negative = backwards)

command : command(t, s, v) -> (drive, brake) (both ≥ 0 [m/s²]. Capped at μ g cos θ and a_max).

It is called with v = 0.0 only while stopped (even if the speed crosses 0 at the midpoint of a moving step, the command receives

±1e-300 in the direction of motion), so the command may write "hold once stopped" with v == 0 / v <= 0.

If the command changes discontinuously in time, put that time in t_breaks so the step is split there (for exactness).

road : road profile (same as road_eval)

t_end : end time [s], dt : step [s]

params : dict from long_params (None = default)

t0 : initial time [s]

Returns

dict : t, s, v, a, drive, brake, z, W_drive, W_brake, W_rr, W_drag (each an (n,) array, a = acceleration at that time),

stopped (bool array), events (list of ("stop"|"move", t, s, 向き)), saturated (whether any step was capped at a limit), params.

Raises ValueError: invalid arguments, command returned a negative or non-finite value.
